title: How I Fell in with the Curate
question: Is there any hope left against them?

shots.frame: Close at sunset on the pale face of the curate (long pale face of fair weakness with a retreating chin and a small full mouth, soot-smudged white linen shirt sleeves under a black clerical waistcoat buttoned to a white anglican dog collar), his large pale blue eyes staring blankly, asking in bewilderment.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward his face until it fills the middle of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; he asks, staring past the lens; his shoulders go on trembling.
shots.camera: level with his eyes, two paces from him, an 85mm lens. The sunset comes from the LEFT; his face reads pale rose and the hedge reads dark
shots.at_rest: The curate is at the CENTRE, turned to the camera, his pale face lit rose from the LEFT, his flaxen curls on his low forehead, the dark hedge behind him at the RIGHT third. His head is half the frame's height.
shots.why: 'What does it mean?' he said. 'What do these things mean?'

shots.frame: Wide in the late afternoon over the great sand pit on Horsell Common, a pillar of green smoke rising from it and one tall fighting-machine standing sentinel on the rim.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the burnt heather until the pillar of green smoke already in the picture stands at the centre, travelling one short stride; the green smoke goes on climbing into the sky; the sentinel's brazen hood goes on turning.
shots.camera: above the heather at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The low sun comes from the west at the LEFT; the sand reads gold and the machine's shadow reads black
shots.at_rest: The raw yellow crater fills the BOTTOM half from the LEFT third to the RIGHT third, the pillar of green smoke rises from its CENTRE to the TOP edge, the sentinel fighting-machine stands on the crater rim at the RIGHT third, and blackened heather with burnt cottages runs to the low horizon across the TOP third at the LEFT. The charred cart lies at the BOTTOM LEFT and the black pine woods stand on the skyline at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.why: The Martians went back to their pit, and a wall of guns rose against them.
source: the Martians retreated to their original position upon Horsell Common
above the blackened heather and ruined buildings that stretched far and wide, stood one as sentinel

sounds.sound: a deep metallic clanking of heavy machinery at work in a pit, far off

shots.frame: Medium in the late afternoon on the empty fighting-machines standing with folded legs on the crater rim, green smoke rising behind them.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the green smoke across to the machines already in the picture until they stand at the centre, travelling a hand's breadth; the green smoke goes on rolling up behind them; sparks go on drifting from the pit.
shots.camera: on the heather at a standing man's eye, a 50mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT; the hoods read brass and the smoke reads green
shots.at_rest: The empty fighting-machines stand at the CENTRE on the crater rim with their long legs folded, the green smoke rising behind them at the TOP third, and a gentle slope of raw yellow sand runs down across the BOTTOM third. The low sun lies gold on their hoods from the LEFT. Their folded tentacles hang slack from under the hoods, and burnt heather edges the rim at the BOTTOM LEFT.
shots.why: They left the machines empty on the rim and went down into the pit.
source: the rest abandoned their vast fighting-machines and descended into the pit

shots.frame: Insert at twilight on the black muzzle of a field gun in the beech shade, a heliograph mirror flashing on a far hill.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the gun wheel to the muzzle already in the picture until the far heliograph stands at the top of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; the heliograph goes on flashing on the far hill; the smoke of the villages goes on drifting over the valley.
shots.camera: low beside the gun wheel, a 50mm lens. The twilight glow comes from the RIGHT; the muzzle reads black and the heliograph reads white
shots.at_rest: The black muzzle of the field gun points out of the beech shade at the CENTRE, its spoked wheel at the BOTTOM LEFT, the twilight valley pale at the RIGHT third, and a heliograph mirror flashing on a far hill at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.why: Scouts with heliographs crawled out to watch for them.
source: every row of suburban villas on the hilly slopes about Kingston and Richmond, masked an expectant black muzzle
crawled the devoted scouts with the heliographs that were presently to warn the gunners

sounds.sound: a heavy iron field gun breech being closed, metal on metal

shots.frame: Medium in the hot afternoon at water level on the steaming Thames, seen from behind, on the head and bare shoulders of the narrator (dark brown hair cut short at back and sides, parted on the left and combed smooth, neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, bare to the waist: torso, back and shoulders streaked black with smoke) wading, reaching for a small abandoned rowing boat.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right along the water, a truck with small amplitude, until the boat already in the picture stands at the centre, travelling one short stride; he goes on swimming toward the boat; the steam goes on drifting over the water.
shots.camera: at the water's surface, a 35mm lens. The hot sun comes from the west at the LEFT; the steam reads white and the water reads green
shots.at_rest: The narrator swims at the CENTRE in the grey-green water with his head and shoulders above it, reaching for the small boat's side at the RIGHT third, white steam drifting across the TOP third. His head is a fifth of the frame's height.
shots.why: I saw an abandoned boat drifting down-stream, and went after it.
source: I saw an abandoned boat, very small and remote, drifting down-stream

sounds.sound: a man swimming, splashing through river water

shots.frame: Insert in the hot afternoon on a scalded bare hand paddling over the side of a small wooden boat in grey-green water.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the gunwale as the boat drifts, a follow with small amplitude, travelling a hand's breadth; the hand goes on paddling through the water; the ripples go on spreading behind it.
shots.camera: low beside the gunwale, a 50mm lens. The hot sun comes from the west at the LEFT; the hand reads red and the water reads green
shots.at_rest: A scalded bare hand paddles at the CENTRE over the side of the small wooden boat, the grey gunwale runs across the LEFT third, the grey-green water fills the RIGHT half with ripples spreading behind the hand, and white steam drifts across the TOP third. The scalded forearm reads raw red against the grey wood, and the ripples run out to the BOTTOM RIGHT.
shots.why: I contrived to paddle, as well as my parboiled hands would allow.
source: I contrived to paddle, as well as my parboiled hands would allow

sounds.sound: a hand paddling in water beside a small wooden boat
